items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Experience managing or coordinating administrative operations, including development and implementation of procedures and business processes.
Experience coordinating administrative activities across functions such as financial services, human resources, facilities, student services, communications, or related operational areas.
Experience developing, analyzing, interpreting, and applying administrative policies and procedures.
Experience coordinating travel and lodging, meetings/conferences, events, purchasing, and travel and entertainment reimbursements in a complex organization.
Experience with analysis of operational information to support planning and decision-making.
Experience administering goal-setting or priority-tracking processes (e.g., OKRs) and related platforms (e.g., Teamflect).
Experience coordinating multiple concurrent administrative projects, meetings, events, or initiatives; setting priorities; resolving issues; and ensuring timely follow-through.
Experience providing executive-level administrative support and working with confidential correspondence and internal/external stakeholders with discretion and sound judgment.

Under the general direction of the Chief Operations & People Officer (COPO) of UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education (CPE), the Administrative Operations Officer uses seasoned administrative operations skills to independently manage, plan, and administer division-level administrative operations and to provide high-level project management, policy, and analytical support that advances the priorities of the Dean and the Division. The position owns the development and continuous improvement of administrative processes and procedures; develops, leads, and analyzes divisional policies and procedures; manages complex and sensitive initiatives from planning through completion; and, on behalf of the Dean, oversees management and tracking of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) and Dean’s Office annual priorities and the division’s Objectives and Key Results (OKR) process in Teamflect, serving as a trusted partner to leadership.

The incumbent independently performs the full range of administrative operations responsibilities for the assigned portfolio, exercising discretion and sound judgment. The position applies and interprets University policies, procedures, and business practices; analyzes operational and policy issues, determines practical solutions, and decides on methods, priorities, and timelines for assigned work, escalating matters that require leadership decision. The position supports short- and long-term operational planning; serves as a resource on operational issues and policies; serves on committees and work groups; prepares analyses, recommendations, reports, and executive and stakeholder communications; and plans and organizes meetings and events. The position also provides backup administrative support to the Dean’s Executive Assistant and participates in division-wide initiatives as assigned.

Familiarity with UC Davis administrative systems and processes, including tools such as AggieBuy, AggieTravel, AggieService, and other systems used for financial, travel, and operational administration.

Thorough knowledge of University or comparable organizational rules, regulations, processes, protocols, and procedures for administrative operations and personnel administration. Knowledge of policy development and analysis, with the ability to interpret policy, assess its operational impact, and determine practical solutions. Strong interpersonal skills, including verbal and written communication, active listening, critical thinking, persuasiveness, advising, and customer service. Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality. Strong skills in short-term planning, analysis, problem-solving, prioritization, and coordination of multiple concurrent assignments.
Ability to adapt to ambiguity, uncertainty, and frequent change in support of executives and program managers.

Thorough knowledge of human resources policies and procedures, with the ability to identify issues and determine practical solutions within established guidelines. Knowledge of a variety of administrative operational activities such as event planning, travel, risk management, facilities/resource coordination, accounting/payroll processes, and related administrative services. Solid knowledge of common University-specific computer applications and demonstrated proficiency with spreadsheets, databases, word processing, presentation software, Box, Zoom, and project/work management tools (e.g., Smartsheet, Airtable). Analytical and problem-solving skills to identify problems and develop solutions. Proven ability to manage complex projects, set priorities, anticipate needs, coordinate multiple details simultaneously, and follow through to successful completion in fast-paced environments.
